# SI prefixes {.unnumbered}

```{=latex}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Prefix & Symbol & Multiplier\\
\midrule
giga & G & $10^9$\\
mega & M & $10^6$\\
kilo & k & $10^3$\\
base & -- & $10^0$\\
milli & m & $10^{-3}$\\
micro & $\mu$ & $10^{-6}$\\
nano & n & $10^{-9}$\\
pico & p & $10^{-12}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

# Notation and significant figures {.unnumbered}

- Scientific notation: $1\leq |a|<10$ in $a\times10^n$.
- Engineering notation uses exponents divisible by 3.
- Multiplication and division: use the fewest significant figures.
- Addition and subtraction: round to the least precise decimal place.
- Keep calculator digits until the final result. Include units.

# GUESS {.unnumbered}

```{=latex}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{cl}
\toprule
Letter & Action\\
\midrule
\textbf{G} & list given symbols, values, units\\
\textbf{U} & name the unknown and target unit\\
\textbf{E} & write and rearrange the equation\\
\textbf{S} & substitute values with units\\
\textbf{S} & solve, round, and state the answer\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

# Ohm's law, power, and energy {.unnumbered}

$$V=IR \qquad I=\frac{V}{R} \qquad R=\frac{V}{I}$$

$$P=VI=I^2R=\frac{V^2}{R}$$

$$E=Pt \qquad Q=It$$

Check component voltage, current, and power ratings.

# Series rules {.unnumbered}

$$I_T=I_1=I_2=\cdots$$

$$V_T=V_1+V_2+\cdots \qquad R_T=R_1+R_2+\cdots$$

One current path. A shared node has no other branch.

# Parallel rules {.unnumbered}

$$V_T=V_1=V_2=\cdots$$

$$I_T=I_1+I_2+\cdots \qquad \frac{1}{R_T}=\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2}+\cdots$$

For two resistors, $R_T=R_1R_2/(R_1+R_2)$.

![Series has one current path; parallel has separate branches across the same two nodes.](../schematics/Series_Parallel_Comparison.pdf){width=100%}

# Kirchhoff's laws {.unnumbered}

**KCL at a node:** $\sum I_{\mathrm{in}}=\sum I_{\mathrm{out}}$

**KVL around a loop:** $\sum V=0$

# Divider and timing relationships {.unnumbered}

$$V_{\mathrm{out}}=V_{\mathrm{in}}\frac{R_2}{R_1+R_2}$$

$$\tau=RC$$

Loading changes the effective divider resistance. One time constant reaches about $63.2\%$ of the final RC step change.

# LED current limiting {.unnumbered}

$$R=\frac{V_S-V_F}{I_{\mathrm{LED}}}$$

$$P_R=I_{\mathrm{LED}}^2R$$

Confirm LED polarity, current, resistor power, and supply limits.

# Transistor switching {.unnumbered}

For an NPN low-side switch:

$$R_B=\frac{V_{\mathrm{drive}}-V_{BE}}{I_B} \qquad I_B\geq\frac{I_C}{\beta_{\mathrm{forced}}}$$

Use a flyback diode across an inductive load. Check device pinout, voltage, current, and power.

# Basic digital logic {.unnumbered}

```{=latex}
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{cl}
\toprule
Notation & Meaning\\
\midrule
$\overline{A}$ & NOT A\\
$AB$ & A AND B\\
$A+B$ & A OR B\\
$A\oplus B$ & A XOR B\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

For $n$ inputs, a complete truth table has $2^n$ rows. Count from all zeros to all ones in binary.

# Stable switch inputs {.unnumbered}

- Pull-down: open reads 0; a switch to $V_{CC}$ reads 1.
- Pull-up: open reads 1; a switch to ground reads 0.
- A switch-to-ground input is usually **active-low**.
- Never leave a CMOS input floating.
- Confirm GPIO logic voltage. Do not assume 5 V tolerance.

# Measurement placement {.unnumbered}

```{=latex}
\begin{center}\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
Instrument & Placement & Power state\\
\midrule
voltmeter & parallel & on\\
ammeter & series & on after setup check\\
ohmmeter & isolated part & off and discharged\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

Never place a current-configured meter directly across a source. Return the red lead from the current jack after measuring.
